item.title: US commerce secy was sent secret memo on Nvidia CEO’s affair with Chinese spy: Report
item.description: US commerce secretary Howard Lutnick had recieved a confidential memo revealing Nvidia's CEO, Jensen Huang's ties to a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The memo was circulated ahead of President Trump's visit to China in May. Although US officials alerted Trump about Huang’s connections, no action was taken, and Huang was invited on the trip. This situation has raised alarms over Huang's role in shaping AI policies and decisions affecting Nvidia.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Coded calls from Brooklyn jail: How Iran operative directed terror plots in Europe, US
item.description: A US indictment alleges that an Iran-backed operative jailed in New York used coded calls with family members to coordinate a plot against RAF Fairford, a British air base housing US troops. The accused and two associates are also alleged to have planned nearly 20 attacks targeting Jewish communities across Europe and the US.

item.title: ‘Unfit to remain in office’: Eisenkot attacks Netanyahu after ‘hateful’ Knesset speech
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party cancelled a meeting with Netanyahu's Likud party after his controversial speech. Eisenkot criticized Netanyahu for his divisive and unfit behavior during the Knesset swearing-in ceremony. Netanyahu continues to advocate for a unity government while rejecting ties with Arab parties. The political landscape remains fragmented with no party holding a clear majority in the Knesset.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: US army officer arrested in UK on suspicion of spying for Russia
item.description: A US army officer serving with Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps was arrested near Gloucester in England on suspicion of espionage linked to Russia, British police said. The 41-year-old suspect faces allegations of assisting a foreign intelligence service and obtaining or disclosing protected information. The arrest comes amid growing European concerns over Russian covert operations, sabotage and espionage targeting Nato countries.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Mishra

item.title: Nvidia hires top US law firm to investigate affair between CEO Huang and Chinese spy
item.description: Nvidia has engaged the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to probe allegations against CEO Jensen Huang, who is implicated in a case involving a suspected Chinese spy named Alice Huang. While Jensen has acknowledged a personal relationship with Alice, he firmly denies any involvement in espionage. The FBI has also launched a separate investigation, but Nvidia reassures all stakeholders that trade secrets and national security remain intact.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Tennessee family wins driveway access but loses lawsuit against city over fence permit
item.description: A Tennessee family regained access to a shared driveway after a neighbour built a fence through it. A state court later confirmed the family's easement and ordered the fence removed. However, a federal judge dismissed their separate lawsuit against the city, ruling that issuing the building permit did not amount to a government taking.

item.title: Iowa Supreme Court overturns foreclosure after lender failed to notify a co-owner of the default
item.description: In a landmark decision, the Iowa Supreme Court determined that Lynae D McMillen Dickey Tesdall, a co-owner of a property, must receive notice before any foreclosure actions can proceed. Despite not signing the promissory note, she was listed as a borrower in the mortgage. While absent, missed payments accumulated, and Wells Fargo neglected to inform her of the ongoing overdue amount.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Old Masters Evening Sale: rare Altdorfer oil emerges after decades; expected to fetch up to £5 million
item.description: An extraordinary Renaissance masterpiece by Albrecht Altdorfer, estimated at £3 million to £5 million, is set for auction. Having been part of a private Swiss collection since 1957, this painting promises to be a rare find. Prior to the auction, it will grace exhibits in both New York and London, showcasing Altdorfer's revolutionary landscapes that brilliantly emphasize nature's significance in art.

item.title: Texas family gets $21.6 million after faulty plumbing makes home unfit to live in
item.description: A Texas family has been awarded more than $21.6 million after faulty plumbing sent sewer gas into their home, which they bought in 2018. A plumber later found that the sewer vents ended in the attic. The family reported health problems and had to leave the house, which remains uninhabitable.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Generation Be There Campaign: Lady Gaga-backed course tops 100,000 learners; skills boost peer support
item.description: Lady Gaga's Born This Way Foundation, collaborating with Jack dot org, has introduced the Be There Certificate programme. This initiative empowers individuals to identify mental health issues and offer necessary support. Since its inception in March 2022, over 100,000 people have successfully completed the complimentary online course. Participants feel more confident in assisting others facing these challenges, promoting a culture of awareness and accountability in mental health welfare.
